conventions.convention: The declared grade m≥1 is part of the polynomial data and may exceed its actual degree. Regular means det P is not identically zero. Homogeneous parameters use λ=α/β and infinity=[1:0]; infinite algebraic multiplicity is the zero order of det P_rev,m at zero.
The companion pencil is L(λ)=A_c−λB_c, with top row (λA_m+A_(m−1),A_(m−2),…,A_0), lower adjacent blocks (−I,λI), and lift (λ^(m−1)x,…,x).

Backward error uses strictly positive weights and independent unrestricted complex coefficient perturbations, measured by the square root of Σ_j ||ΔA_j||_F²/ω_j², with the parameter and nonzero vector fixed.

The rational domain excludes poles of every reduced entry; q is the monic least common multiple of reduced denominators. Rational eigenpairs require λ in that domain, even if qR is singular at an excluded pole.
Residual transfer uses finite λ, recovers x=z_m, and interprets empty sums as zero for m=1.

load_bearing.statement: For regular square grade-m P, the first companion pencil admits unimodular equivalence to diag(P,I), and its reversal admits unimodular equivalence to diag(P_rev,m,I). Its determinant equals det P; finite eigenvectors correspond by the companion lift, infinite eigenvectors by x↦(x,0,…,0) from ker A_m, and infinite algebraic multiplicity is mn−deg det P.

Under the weighted-backward-error definition's hypotheses, S=Σ_j ω_j²|α|^(2j)|β|^(2(m−j))>0, the infimum is attained, and η_F=||P_h(α,β)x||₂/(||x||₂√S). At infinity this is ||A_mx||₂/(ω_m||x||₂); reversal uses weights ω_(m−k).
For any block vector z with e=L(λ)z and x=z_m, P(λ)x=e_1+Σ_(k=2)^m Q_k(λ)e_k, where Q_k(λ)=Σ_(j=m−k+1)^m A_j λ^(j−m+k−1); consequently ||P(λ)x||₂≤||e_1||₂+Σ_(k=2)^m ||Q_k(λ)||_F||e_k||₂.
For every λ∈Ω and every nonzero x, R(λ)x=0 if and only if N(λ)x=0. No point outside Ω is a rational eigenvalue, regardless of whether N is singular there.
